_doc.title: Accord Retail Ontology — Knowledge Base
_doc.purpose: Machine-readable ontology. Every object type, evidence type, decision, verb and link the analysis engine reads to make decisions and enforce governance.
conventions: Keys beginning with '_' are documentation only. The engine must ignore them.
Enum values are lower_snake_case for data values and UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for verbs, decision types and outcomes.
'mutates' and 'performed_by' are always arrays. A read-only verb has mutates: [] and read_only: true.
Evidence types are referenced everywhere by their 'name'. Decisions list the evidence names they read.
This file is versioned with the ontology. A change to objects, evidence types, decisions, verbs or links requires a version bump.
reconciliations: RECOMMENDATION_ASSESSMENT outcome is ASSESSED | CANNOT_ASSESS. RECOMMENDED | NOT_RECOMMENDED is the per-action verdict inside an ASSESSED outcome. EXECUTE_ACTION is entitled by outcome = ASSESSED and verdict = RECOMMENDED (see GOVERNANCE.md §14).
cart_abandonment_rate is included as the 20th evidence type, carried over from the ontology document, so the count matches the declared 20 across 5 categories.

model._comment: Five collections: objects (what exists), evidence_types (what can be known), decisions (what can be concluded), verbs (what can be done), links (how objects relate).

objects.name: Business
objects.business_meaning: The retail owner's business unit; data scope boundary

properties.name: goals
properties.description: Free text: what does owner want to achieve

properties.name: fiscal_year_start
properties.description: Jan, Feb, etc. for seasonal normalization

objects.name: Product
objects.business_meaning: A sellable item (SKU) with stable identity

objects.name: Sale
objects.business_meaning: A transaction; the fact that a product was sold

objects.name: Customer
objects.business_meaning: Cohort of buyers (never individuals; aggregated only)

objects.name: Evidence
objects.business_meaning: A sourced statement about the business (revenue, churn, margin, etc.)
objects.description: Evidence is never computed invisibly. Every statement has provenance.

properties.name: evidence_type
properties.description: Must match a name in model.evidence_types

properties.name: state
properties.description: Has this evidence been observed, is it missing, or does it conflict?

objects.name: Decision
objects.business_meaning: An auditable conclusion reached against declared inputs
objects.description: Every decision is deterministic. Same inputs always produce same outcome.

properties.name: outcome
properties.description: Valid values depend on decision_type; see model.decisions[].outcomes

properties.name: input_digest
properties.description: SHA256 hash of Evidence inputs for replay/reproducibility

objects.name: Action
objects.business_meaning: Something done in the world, authorized by a decision outcome

evidence_types.name: revenue_monthly
evidence_types.calculation: SUM(sales.revenue) WHERE sale_date >= month_start AND sale_date < month_end
evidence_types.description: Total revenue this month (aggregated, not by customer)

evidence_types.name: churn_rate
evidence_types.description: % of customers who didn't return

evidence_types.name: repeat_purchase_rate
evidence_types.calculation: COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id WHERE repeat_count >= 2) / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)
evidence_types.description: % of customers who bought more than once

evidence_types.name: product_margin
evidence_types.description: Gross margin % per product

evidence_types.name: product_revenue_pct
evidence_types.description: What % of total revenue does this product represent

evidence_types.name: inventory_turnover
evidence_types.description: How many times inventory sold and replaced

evidence_types.name: slow_moving_inventory_pct
evidence_types.description: % of working capital tied up in slow-moving stock

evidence_types.name: customer_lifetime_value
evidence_types.description: Average total revenue per customer over their lifetime

evidence_types.name: customer_acquisition_cost
evidence_types.description: Average cost to acquire one customer (by channel)

evidence_types.name: ltv_to_cac_ratio
evidence_types.description: Unit economics health: 3:1 or higher is healthy

evidence_types.name: revenue_concentration
evidence_types.description: What % of revenue comes from top 3 products (concentration risk)

evidence_types.name: channel_mix
evidence_types.description: Revenue distribution across channels

evidence_types.name: margin_trend
evidence_types.description: Is margin getting better or worse month-over-month

evidence_types.name: revenue_trend
evidence_types.description: Month-over-month growth rate

evidence_types.name: customer_cohort_retention
evidence_types.description: Which acquisition channel has best repeat rate

evidence_types.name: stockout_frequency
evidence_types.calculation: How many times did a product run out of stock
evidence_types.description: Revenue lost to stockouts (proxy: customer counts unable to buy)

evidence_types.name: cart_abandonment_rate
evidence_types.calculation: abandoned_carts / initiated_checkouts * 100 (owner-supplied from e-commerce platform analytics)
evidence_types.description: Conversion leak for online channels; absent for in-store-only businesses

evidence_types.name: competitor_price_comparison
evidence_types.description: How does our pricing compare to competitors

evidence_types.name: industry_churn_benchmark
evidence_types.calculation: Industry average churn rate for this retail category
evidence_types.description: Benchmark to assess if our churn is abnormal

evidence_types.name: industry_margin_benchmark
evidence_types.calculation: Industry average gross margin for this category
evidence_types.description: Benchmark to assess if our margin is abnormal

decisions.name: BOTTLENECK_DIAGNOSIS
decisions.subject: Business
decisions.question: What is the #1 constraint limiting this business's growth?

outcomes.meaning: The diagnosis succeeded; a bottleneck was found

data.bottleneck_type: string, enum: [churn, margin, inventory, concentration, ltv_cac, channel]

outcomes.meaning: Required evidence is missing or contradicted; cannot diagnose

decisions.determinism: Same Evidence inputs must produce same outcome. Deterministic hash of inputs stored for auditability.

decisions.name: RECOMMENDATION_ASSESSMENT
decisions.subject: Bottleneck + Business context
decisions.question: For this bottleneck, what are the top 3 actions to take?

outcomes.meaning: Bottleneck identified but sizing evidence is missing; recommendations cannot be ranked

decisions.determinism: Same bottleneck + same evidence = same recommendations

verbs.name: SUBMIT_DATA
verbs.label: Submit form or CSV data
verbs.description: Business owner enters data via form or uploads CSV

verbs.name: ANALYZE
verbs.label: Run BOTTLENECK_DIAGNOSIS
verbs.description: Platform ingests Evidence and runs diagnosis (async job)

verbs.name: PROPOSE_ACTIONS
verbs.label: Generate recommendations
verbs.description: Platform runs RECOMMENDATION_ASSESSMENT and ranks top 3

verbs.name: PUBLISH_REPORT
verbs.label: Generate and deliver monthly report
verbs.description: Render diagnosis + recommendations + measurement framework as PDF/HTML

verbs.name: VIEW_REPORT
verbs.label: Business owner views report
verbs.description: Read-only access to monthly report and audit trail

verbs.name: EXECUTE_ACTION
verbs.label: Business owner takes an action
verbs.entitled_by: RECOMMENDATION_ASSESSMENT outcome = ASSESSED and action verdict = RECOMMENDED
verbs.description: Owner implements a recommended action (e.g., loyalty program, price change)

verbs.name: RECORD_OUTCOME
verbs.label: Business owner reports results
verbs.description: Owner enters outcome metrics (e.g., churn improved 3%) → becomes new Evidence

verbs.name: CONNECT_SHOPIFY
verbs.label: Grant OAuth permission to Shopify
verbs.description: Owner grants Accord access to Shopify data

links.enforces: A product belongs to exactly one business
Every sale belongs to one business

links.meaning: A business has many customer cohorts
links.enforces: Every customer belongs to one business

links.meaning: Each sale is of one product
links.enforces: A sale cannot reference multiple products

links.meaning: Each sale is to one customer
Evidence is always scoped to an object
links.enforces: Evidence is never free-floating; always has a subject

links.meaning: A decision reads multiple evidence types
links.enforces: Decision stores which Evidence version it read (for replay)

links.meaning: An action requires a decision outcome to execute
links.enforces: No action without authorization; roles alone never sufficient
Closes the loop: Evidence has provenance (action behind it)

governance._comment: rules are invariants the engine must enforce; entitlements map roles to the verbs they may perform. A role permits participation; only a decision outcome entitles a consequential verb.

rules.enforcement: Same Evidence inputs → same outcome. input_digest validates this.

rules.rule: Every evidence type has source and calculation rule
rules.enforcement: Evidence never computed invisibly. asserted_by and source_system always declared.
If two evidence sources disagree (state=contradicted), decision returns CANNOT_DECIDE and names the conflict.
confidence < 0.7 → decision includes reason (missing data, low sample size).

rules.rule: Every action requires a decision outcome
rules.enforcement: authorized_by_decision_id never NULL for consequential actions. Roles alone never authorize.
If data missing, decision returns CANNOT_DECIDE and names the gap. Never extrapolate from thin data.
Every query filtered by business_id at database layer. No cross-tenant data leakage. Critical from Phase 3 (multi-tenant).
audit_log is append-only. No deletes, no updates. Entry per action.

entitlements.scope: clients' businesses only (if granted access by owner)
all tenants (but queries filtered by business_id)
